newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE dips in third day of quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE dips in third day of quiet trade.

text.p: Spot MTBE prices dipped in the third consecutive day of quiet trade on Wednesday amid a tail off in bids and a gain in confidence over the supply pool for August.
"There is still not a lot of MTBE out there but all the U.S. Gulf producers are up and running and supply looks a lot better for the second half of August," said a USG trader.
In late trade on Tuesday, refiners bought two parcels at 96.50 cents, bringing down sellers to about 96.25 cents on Wednesday. Sellers were about 0.75 cent below midday Tuesday levels.
New York Harbor was pegged about a penny under Tuesday at 100.00/102.00 cents in quiet trade.

Players said values were done mostly because of the lack of enquiries. Supply for prompt July and first half August remain very tight due as the market plays catch-up following a a spate of production problems in the past two to three months.
